issues.failure_explanation: The proofs of glothm (via Lemma lm1's coercivity), lem1 (term $I_4$), lem2, prop:exponential decay, cea (continuity estimate), and thm:main local all invoke the resolution condition \cref{eq:res}, $C_1\mu_{\mathup{msh}}^{-1}k^2H^2\leq C_*\Lambda$, but none of these results lists it (or any mesh-wavenumber restriction) among its hypotheses: glothm states only $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ (and not even the large-contrast regime), and prop:exponential decay/thm:main local state only \cref{ass:overlapping} plus the contrast/eigenvalue ranges. As stated, the conclusions are asserted for arbitrary $k$ and $H$; for large $k^2H^2$ the absorption of the $k^2$-term that every proof relies on cannot be performed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the resolution condition \cref{eq:res} (and the standing large-contrast regime) as an explicit hypothesis to glothm, lem1, lem2, prop:exponential decay, cea, and thm:main local.
issues.overall_effect: Every decay, well-posedness, and error statement in the analysis section is formally asserted without the mesh-wavenumber hypothesis its proof needs.
issues.title: Analysis results omit the resolution-condition hypothesis their proofs require
issues.why_classification: Adding the already-introduced standing hypothesis to the statements is a standard local condition; the method, conclusions, rates, and advertised scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The multiscale space entering \cref{cemvar} is defined by \cref{msbasis1} through local problems on the standard oversampling domains $K_i^m$, but every analytic step - well-posedness of the local operator \cref{eq:new local operator}, the decay results lem1/lem2/prop:exponential decay, the inf-sup argument in cea, and the choice $v_{\mathup{ms}}=\hat{\mathcal{G}}^m\psi$ in the proof of thm:main local - uses the symmetrized patches $\hat{K}_i^m$, which the text explicitly states differ from $K_i^m$. No argument identifies $\phi_{i,m}^j$ with $\hat{\mathcal{G}}_i^m\psi_i^j$ or transfers the estimates between the two; in particular $v_{\mathup{ms}}=\hat{\mathcal{G}}^m\psi$ is not shown to belong to $V_{\mathup{ms}}$, and the existence proof promised for \cref{msbasis1} is only given for the hatted problem. The proofs therefore establish well-posedness and the error estimate for a method built from the symmetrized local problems, not for the method defined in \cref{msbasis1}/\cref{cemvar} and used in the numerical section.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the multiscale basis \cref{msbasis1} using the symmetrized local problems \cref{eq:new local operator} so that the analyzed and defined methods coincide (or add a comparison lemma transferring the decay and inf-sup estimates between the two local problems); all estimates then apply to the corrected method.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem and the Cea lemma are proved for the hatted (symmetrized) scheme; the stated conclusions about the scheme actually defined and implemented are unsupported.
issues.title: Analysis is performed on symmetrized patches while the method is defined on standard oversampling domains
issues.why_classification: The repair realigns the method's definition with the analysis - a contained definitional change that preserves every estimate for the corrected method - but as written the main theorem does not cover the scheme it states, and no simple added condition closes the gap, since the failure of T-coercivity on standard patches is the paper's stated reason for symmetrization.
